title: Design a Deterministic Simulation Testing (DST) Harness for Distributed Consensus
prompt: Design a Deterministic Simulation Testing (DST) harness capable of running 100,000 simulated cluster-hours/day across a 5-node Raft key-value store, injecting asymmetric partitions, disk bit-flips, and fsync stalls while checking linearizability and shrinking failing traces.

spark.summary: Build a stateless parallel seed-runner fleet over a syscall-abstracted Raft engine, paired with a fault-injection matrix, linearizability oracle, and delta-debugging trace reducer.
spark.keyTakeaway: To keep the architecture evolvable without sacrificing reliability, run the exact same production Raft state-machine code against a swappable `SimIO` trait so simulation bugs directly expose real production bugs.
spark.byteSummary:
If your simulator tests a toy re-implementation instead of production code, it misses real bugs. A production DST harness defines a clean `RuntimeIO` interface (clock, TCP transport, NVMe disk, RNG) implemented by `RealIO` in production and `SimIO` in tests.

A fleet of stateless CI workers sweeps 100,000+ random 64-bit seeds/day, injecting asymmetric partitions, packet reordering, power-loss uncommitted-page corruption, and clock skew. After each run, a **Linearizability / Property Oracle** checks that no committed write was lost and no split-brain occurred.

When a seed fails, **Delta-Debugging** minimizes the fault schedule down to the smallest sequence of partitions/crashes for 1-click developer reproduction.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Design a Deterministic Simulation Testing (DST) Harness for Distributed Consensus without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: To keep the architecture evolvable without sacrificing reliability, run the exact same production Raft state-machine code against a swappable `SimIO` trait so simulation bugs directly expose real production bugs.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

prerequisites.title: Harness Engineering: Deterministic Simulation Testing & Virtualized Clocks
prerequisites.summary: Deterministic Simulation Testing (DST) replaces all non-deterministic OS syscalls—clocks, network sockets, disk I/O, and PRNG—with a single-seeded deterministic event loop so distributed bugs reproduce bit-for-bit.

prerequisites.title: Consistency & Consensus Replication (Raft / Paxos)
prerequisites.summary: Fault-tolerant replication protocols (Raft, Multi-Paxos, Quorum) that keep distributed state consistent across node crashes and network partitions using majority quorums (2f+1) and monotonic term numbers.

prerequisites.title: Clock Skew & NTP Backward Jumps: Monotonic Timers vs. Wall-Clock Leases
prerequisites.summary: Wall-clock timestamps (time.time() / System.currentTimeMillis()) can jump backward or forward during NTP steps; local timers must use CLOCK_MONOTONIC while distributed leases require server-side TTLs and monotonic fencing tokens.
